details.label: Summary
details.text: Widely scattered, high-based thunderstorms will pose an isolated risk for damaging wind gusts this afternoon

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Supported by ascent ahead of an upper-level low noted in recent satellite imagery off of the central California coastline and an enhanced, mid-level moisture plume downstream of this feature, widely scattered thunderstorms have developed across portions of southern NV into the Low Desert of CA/AZ as of 2030 UTC. Modifying the 18 UTC VEF observed sounding for current surface observations depicts steep low-level lapse rates, a well-mixed boundary layer with LCLs around 3 km AGL, and ~1000 J/kg MLCAPE. While effective shear and deep-layer flow remain weak (per the ESX VWP), favorable thermodynamic profiles for evaporative cooling and downdraft accelerations will promote a risk for damaging/severe wind gusts across the region. Watch issuance is not anticipated, however, owing to the expected isolated nature of the severe risk

details.label: Most probable threats
details.text: MOST PROBABLE PEAK WIND GUST...55-70 MPH

details.label: Summary
details.text: Scattered, initially high-based thunderstorms are expected to develop along and east of the Front Range over the next couple of hours. These storms will evolve eastward through this evening, bringing a threat for severe wind gusts and large hail

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Aided by forcing for ascent ahead of a mid-level perturbation and along/ahead of a surface stationary/cold front, scattered thunderstorm development is expected along the Front Range from southeastern Wyoming into northern Colorado over the next 1-2 hours. Storms will be initially high-based given hot temperatures and well-mixed boundary layer profiles (low-90s F temperatures amid dewpoints in the mid-40s) ahead of the aforementioned surface boundary. While effective shear around 35-40 kts will be sufficient for supercell structures, high cloud bases (LCLs of 2+ km AGL) and steep low-level lapse rates will favor efficient evaporative cooling, downdraft formation, and upscale growth/clustering as convection evolves eastward. Severe wind gusts (a few significant) will be the main threat with this activity, but large to very large hail is also expected, especially early in the convective cycle and with any convection that is able to maintain a discrete mode. A Severe Thunderstorm Watch will likely be needed for at least a portion of the discussion area in the next 1-2 hours to cover these threats

details.label: Most probable threats
details.text: MOST PROBABLE PEAK WIND GUST...65-80 MPH · MOST PROBABLE PEAK HAIL SIZE...1.50-2.50 IN
